rows: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
10% of US adults; higher in Hispanic, Black, Native American populations
Obesity (BMI >30), sedentary lifestyle, family history, age >45, PCOS, gestational diabetes
Often asymptomatic early; polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, weight loss, blurred vision, slow wound healing
Fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dL (x2), HbA1c ≥6.5%, OGTT 2-hr glucose ≥200 mg/dL, random glucose ≥200 + symptoms
Elevated glucose, HbA1c, lipid panel, microalbuminuria, CMP for renal function
Lifestyle modification (diet, exercise), metformin first-line, add SGLT2i/GLP-1 if CVD/CKD, insulin if needed
Hypertension (Essential)
Nearly 50% of US adults; increases with age
Age, obesity, high sodium diet, alcohol use, smoking, stress, family history, Black race
Usually asymptomatic (silent killer); severe: headache, dizziness, vision changes, chest pain
BP ≥130/80 on 2+ occasions; 24-hr ambulatory BP monitoring if white coat suspected
BMP (K+ baseline), urinalysis (proteinuria), lipid panel, ECG (LVH)
Lifestyle: DASH diet, weight loss, exercise, limit alcohol; Meds: ACEi/ARB, CCB, thiazide diuretic
Hyperlipidemia
~40% of adults have elevated LDL; major CVD risk factor
Diet high in saturated fat, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, diabetes, hypothyroidism, family history
Asymptomatic; may present with xanthomas, corneal arcus if severe familial hyperlipidemia
Lipid panel: Total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides; calculate ASCVD risk score
Lipid panel (fasting preferred for TG accuracy), TSH, HbA1c, LFTs before statin
High-intensity statin if LDL ≥190 or ASCVD risk ≥20%; moderate-intensity if 10-year risk 7.5-20%
Heart Failure (Systolic/HFrEF)
6+ million US adults; leading cause of hospitalization in elderly
CAD, MI, HTN, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, diabetes, obesity, alcohol abuse
Dyspnea (exertional → rest), orthopnea, PND, peripheral edema, fatigue, JVD, S3 gallop, pulmonary rales
Echocardiogram (EF <40%), BNP/NT-proBNP, CXR (pulmonary edema, cardiomegaly), ECG
Elevated BNP (>100)/NT-proBNP (>300), BMP (renal function, K+), troponin if ACS suspected
ACEi/ARB + beta blocker + MRA; SGLT2i; diuretics for volume; consider ARNI, ivabradine, hydralazine-nitrate
Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
15% of US adults; higher in elderly, diabetics, hypertensive patients
Diabetes (leading cause), hypertension, glomerulonephritis, PKD, chronic obstruction, NSAIDs
Often asymptomatic until advanced; fatigue, nausea, decreased urine output, edema, uremia symptoms in ESRD
eGFR <60 for >3 months, albuminuria (ACR >30 mg/g), renal ultrasound, biopsy if unclear etiology
Elevated Cr, decreased eGFR, elevated BUN, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, anemia, hyperphosphatemia
Control BP/DM, ACEi/ARB, SGLT2i, dietary restriction (protein, K+, PO4), erythropoietin, dialysis/transplant if ESRD
COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)
16+ million diagnosed in US; 3rd leading cause of death
Smoking (#1 cause - 85-90%), occupational exposures (coal, silica), alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
Chronic cough, sputum production, progressive dyspnea, wheezing, barrel chest, decreased breath sounds
Spirometry: FEV1/FVC <0.70 post-bronchodilator; CXR (hyperinflation, flattened diaphragm), CT if bullae/emphysema
Spirometry (obstructive pattern), CBC (polycythemia), ABG (hypoxemia, hypercapnia in severe)
Smoking cessation, bronchodilators (SABA/LABA, anticholinergics), ICS if frequent exacerbations, O2 if hypoxemic, pulmonary rehab
